sources: MS NOW, Oct 30, citing three senior Persian Gulf Arab officials (anonymity); relayed by TOI liveblog 04:54 IST Oct 31, Clash Report, Political Wire, Longbridge
fault_line: Is a Nov 4 strike date a real war plan, or election-calendar politics -- a strike timed to avoid midterm accountability, or a deal deadline Tehran must beat?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- MS NOW, single outlet for the new elements] Trump plans to resume strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms, 'as early as November 4', after his administration briefed Gulf allies to prepare for 'a short, intense round of attacks'. Gulf allies are pushing de-escalation over Iranian retaliation fears; one Gulf official said some Gulf states might resist US strikes launched from bases on their soil. New details in the same report: Trump has named Pickaxe Mountain (deeply buried nuclear-linked site) as a possible target; a third carrier strike group (USS Theodore Roosevelt, ~9,000 sailors/Marines) is en route, arriving end of November; Qatar proposed a seven-day confidence-building plan with envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff involved. [VERIFIED FACT -- prior backbone] WSJ Oct 27 first reported the post-midterm briefing and AP confirmed it Oct 28 via two diplomats -- but neither carried the Nov 4 date. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- White House] A White House official declined to comment on military plans: Trump 'keeps all options on the table' to prevent an Iranian nuclear weapon. [VERIFIED FACT] No final strike decision has been announced; the US has not struck Iran since Sept 1 and Trump pledged no strikes before the midterms. [COUNTERPOINT] Trump himself said Friday the war will be 'wrapped up soon' (KCMO, covered 0300-03) -- the same 24 hours carry both a deal ending and a Nov 4 strike date.
sections.what_verified: The post-midterm short-intense-campaign briefing is corroborated by 2 tiered families (WSJ T2, AP T1, Oct 27-28). The NOVEL elements -- the Nov 4 date, Pickaxe Mountain, Roosevelt sailing, Qatar seven-day plan -- rest on MS NOW alone, and MS NOW has NO declared tier in the registry, so it NEVER counts toward corroboration. family_count below counts only tiered families for the briefing element; the Nov 4 date itself is single-source (untiered) and must be reported as 'MS NOW reports', never as fact.
sections.what_disputed: White House declined to confirm plans; Trump publicly says the war will end soon and that he is in no rush for a deal; no final decision announced (MS NOW itself, AP). Sen. Chris Murphy, after a classified briefing, called a restart 'insane' (per the in-window Aaron Parnas reel citing Murphy -- social relay, not a primary quote retrieved).
sections.why_matters: A date is now on the war: MS NOW reports Trump was briefed to resume Iran strikes as early as November 4 -- the day after the midterms -- while in the same 24 hours he says the war will be 'wrapped up soon'. Which one is the plan?
